section_title: What made the Macedonian churches so eager to help?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 1 Now, brothers, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the churches of Macedonia. 2 In the terrible ordeal they suffered, their abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity. 3 For I testify that they gave according to their ability and even beyond it. Of their own accord,

4 they earnestly pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints. 5 And not only did they do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, through the will of God.

context_lines: Paul turns from the restored relationship with Corinth to the collection for believers in need. [1 Corinthians 16:1–4](https://biblehub.com/bsb/1_corinthians/16.htm) and [Romans 15:25–27](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/15.htm) identify the wider undertaking as help for the saints in Jerusalem. Here he begins with the example of the churches in Macedonia.

They were experiencing a terrible ordeal and deep poverty. Yet their abundant joy overflowed into rich generosity. Paul introduces their response as evidence of grace God has given them, so the story begins with His work among them.

Their contribution was willing. They gave according to their ability and beyond it, eagerly asking for the privilege of sharing in this service. Paul reports their extraordinary response without naming an amount or assigning everyone the same percentage.
Their giving grew out of giving themselves first to the Lord and then to the workers, through God’s will. The material gift expressed a deeper commitment to Him and to the good of His people.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand this as willing generosity flowing from God’s grace and a wholehearted commitment to Him. [Wesley’s notes on verses 1–5](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-second-epistle-to-the-corinthians/) and the [USCCB notes on verses 1–5](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/2corinthians/8) both emphasize the Macedonians’ eagerness and the giving of themselves. Their poverty and joy are both real parts of the account.
god_plan_lines: [Acts 4:32–35](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/4.htm) describes the early Jerusalem believers sharing resources so that people’s needs were met. The collection here carries that care across the distance between congregations.

[Romans 15:26–27](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/15.htm) also explains the connection between Gentile believers and the Jewish believers they are helping. God’s work of bringing people together in Christ takes practical form when those who share spiritual blessings also share material help.
